venue.name: Cowichan Bay Maritime Centre & Cowichan Wooden Boat Society
venue.description: The Cowichan Bay Maritime Centre is a community maritime museum run by the Cowichan Wooden Boat Society, a non-profit that began in the 1980s as a wooden boat building workshop. The heart of it is a 100 metre heritage pier carrying three themed pods: a canoe shed with dugout canoes built with Quw'utsun' elders and cultural advisors, an interactive pod with a ship's helm, pulleys, knot tying and a kids boatbuilding booth, and a shack of restored vintage inboard and outboard motors. At the end of the pier the Supercargoes Pavilion holds an exhibit on traditional small wooden boats, and an outdoor Patio Portal has tables, benches and a children's interactive tug. Admission is listed as $5 for adults and $3 for children, and the Centre also runs summer day camps for children and boatbuilding courses.
venue.address: 1761 Cowichan Bay Rd., Cowichan Bay, BC V0R 1N0

facility_notes.lunch_space: The mezzanine floor of our main museum building offers a charming and versatile space for private functions, accommodating up to 65 guests. It is rented by the hour rather than open to visitors.

venue.price_year_or_season: The children's camp fee of $275 a week is the 2026 summer season rate. The $5 and $3 admission and the workshop and rental rates carry no year on the site.

programs.name: Self-guided museum and pier visit
programs.description: A walk out along the 100 metre heritage pier and through the museum. The first pod is the Snuhwulh'e'w't-hw canoe shed with dugout canoes and the history of the canoe, built with elders Wayne Paige and Dr Luschiim Charlie and cultural advisor Diane Hinkley. The second pod is the hands-on one, with a ship's helm to stand at, pulleys, knot tying and the kids boatbuilding booth where a child can build a small wooden boat to take home. The third is the Seagull Shack of restored classic inboard and outboard motors, and the Supercargoes Pavilion at the end holds the Ship's Boats and Handliners exhibit. Admission is listed as $5 adult and $3 child, with no group rate published.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the length of the pier and go into each of the three pods. They can step up onto a ship's helm, work pulleys, try knot tying and build a small wooden boat to take home at the boatbuilding booth. Outside on the patio there is a children's interactive tug to climb on.
programs.our_note: The pier is most of the visit and it is outdoors, so check the forecast and note that they close the pier when it is icy or snowy. Their own pages give three different sets of opening days, so phone before you set out rather than turning up. The admission is low but there is no group rate published, so ask about that on the same call.
programs.practical_summary: Admission is $5 for adults and $3 for children, and a good part of the visit is outdoors on a pier. Washrooms, indoor lunch space, bus parking and stroller access are not stated anywhere, so they are worth a call.

programs.name: Field trip visit
programs.description: Field trips are named on the children's programs page as one of the things the Centre runs, alongside the Len Mayea Boatbuilding Booth and the Junior Captains camps. Nothing else about them is published: no length, no ages, no price, no group size, no lead time and no booking form. The page asks you to email cwbs@classicboats.org to ask about any of the children's programs. The boatbuilding course page separately mentions teaching school children the art of boat building in their workshop.
programs.our_note: Field trips are listed but not one detail about them is published, so this is a phone call rather than a form. Ask what a booked visit actually includes, whether the boatbuilding booth runs for a group, how many children they can take and what it costs. Ask about washrooms and somewhere to eat at the same time, because neither is stated.
programs.practical_summary: Nothing about a field trip is published, so length, ages, price, group size and lead time all have to be asked. Washrooms and indoor lunch space are not stated either, and much of the site is outdoors on a pier.
programs.evidence: host to many different children’s events and activities, including our popular ‘Len Mayea Boatbuilding Booth’, Junior Captain Camps, Field Trips

programs.name: Junior Captains Camp
programs.description: A week long summer day camp at the Cowichan Bay seaside. Campers go to the beach, crab, row the Centre's wooden boats, go out in the Cowichan Search and Rescue boat, learn basic woodworking, play nautical games and do crafts. Camps run 9am to 4pm daily with no early drop off or late pickup, and only whole weeks are accepted, with no partial weeks or drop in days. The fee is $275 a week for each child, with family and sibling discounts that are not priced. The camp is aimed at ages 5 to 9 and a five year old must have finished a year of kindergarten, and one listed week is set aside for ages 9 to 12. All eight weeks listed for 2026 ran between early July and early September and all but one are marked full. Registration is by downloading a form and emailing it back, with full payment due at the same time.
programs.what_children_do: Spend the day between the shore and the boats. They walk down to the beach, drop crab lines, take an oar in one of the wooden rowing boats, ride in the search and rescue boat, use basic woodworking tools and play nautical games.
programs.our_note: This is a week long camp that families register a child into one at a time, not something a daycare books as a group. It runs 9 to 4 with no early drop off or late pickup, and the whole week has to be paid when you register. Almost every 2026 week was already marked full, so ask about next summer rather than this one.
programs.practical_summary: Nine to four each day, whole weeks only, $275 a child a week, ages 5 to 9. Washrooms, indoor space and what happens in bad weather are not stated, so ask when you register.
programs.extra_fees_note: Camps are $275/week with family/sibling discounts available. The discount amount is not published.
programs.payment_timing: Full payment is due at time of registration.
programs.evidence: Camps are $275/week with family/sibling discounts available.

programs.name: Annual Traditional Boatbuilding Course
programs.description: Two consecutive five day working weeks, 9am to 5pm daily, building a Tyee lapstrake rowboat with instructor Mark Reuten in the Centre's boatbuilding shop. The course runs from setting up a mould through planking, steam bending and finishing, and the finished boat is raffled to support the Centre. No tools and no experience are needed. The fee is $2,000 with a $1,000 deposit at registration, refundable other than a $100 processing fee for late cancellations after 1 September, and the balance due by the same date. The dates given are 11 to 15 January and 18 to 22 January, with no year stated, and no minimum age is published.
programs.our_note: This is a two week, $2,000 commitment aimed at people who want to build a boat, not a school outing. No minimum age is published, so ask directly if you are thinking of an older teenager. The dates are given without a year and the payment deadline has already gone by, so confirm both before sending money.
programs.practical_summary: Ten full days in a working boat shop, 9am to 5pm, at $2,000 with half of it due at registration. There is no age guidance and no year on the dates, so both need confirming.
programs.payment_timing: A $1,000 deposit is due at time of registration. Full course Balance must be paid by Sept 1st.
programs.cancellation_note: Refundable (other than a $100 processing fee for late cancels after Sept 1st). If the Centre cancels the course, all fees will be refunded in full.
programs.evidence: $2,000. A $1,000 deposit is due at time of registration.

gaps: Admission is not by donation. The footer states $5 adult and $3 child, with no year and no group, school or daycare rate anywhere on the site.
Field trips are named on the children's programs page but nothing about them is published: no length, ages, price, group size, lead time or booking route beyond the general email.
Opening days contradict themselves on the site. Recorded in conflicts, and opening hours are left blank as a result.
Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
Bus parking, coach drop off and stroller or wheelchair access on the pier are not mentioned. The pier is a heritage structure, so access is worth asking about directly.

Indoor lunch space is only described as a paid hourly rental of the mezzanine, from $10 to $60 an hour depending on who you are and when. Whether a visiting group may simply eat somewhere is not stated.
How many adults have to come with a children's group is not stated.
All eight 2026 Junior Captains camp weeks listed had already run or were running by the date of this check, and seven of the eight are marked full. Next year's dates are not published.
The boatbuilding course dates of 11 to 15 January and 18 to 22 January carry no year, and the 1 September payment deadline on the same page has already passed.
The Wooden Boat Festival is still listed for Saturday June 27th, 2026, which has already gone by.
The Wooden Boat Tours page is virtual only. It is a set of videos of visitors' boats, not a tour you can book.
The rowing boat fleet is for members only, so a visiting group cannot take a boat out without joining.

The Open Graph image on every page is the Centre's logo rather than a photograph, so the hero was taken from the home page banner instead. Every photograph on the site has a filename in place of alt text, so the alt lines here were written after looking at the images.

One says every day, one says Wednesday to Sunday with Monday and Tuesday closed, and one says every day in summer. Closing time is 4pm in all of them. Phone before you go.
